title: The Chamalières Tablet
subtitle: A curse from a sacred spring — MAPONOS ARVERNORIGIIS and sixty words of invocation.
objectives: Understand the context of the Chamalières defixio: a sacred spring, a ritual deposit.
Translate the opening: ANDEDION VEDIIUMI DIIIUIOMI.
Parse MAPONOS ARVERNORIGIIS ("Maponos of the Arverni kings").
Recognize the repetition RISVM RISVM VEDIIUMÍ as a ritual formula.

sections.heading: Discovery and context
sections.body: In 1971, during excavations at the Source des Roches in Chamalières (Puy-de-Dôme, central France), archaeologists uncovered a lead tablet inscribed with sixty words of Gaulish text. The tablet was found in a sacred spring, a site where Gauls made offerings to water deities. The spring was active from the 1st century BCE to the 3rd century CE. The tablet dates to around 50 CE, within living memory of Caesar's conquest. The text is a curse or a binding spell.

sections.heading: The opening lines
sections.body:
Here is the beginning of the Chamalières Tablet:

ANDEDION VEDIIUMI DIIIUIOMI RISVM RISVM VEDIIUMÍ AVDMON AVOTÓN MAPONOS ARVERNORIGIIS

Transliteration and parsing:
ANDEDION — "great god" or "very divine" (accusative or vocative, compound: ANDE- "very" + -DION "god")
VEDIIUMI — uncertain; possibly dative of a name or epithet, "to Vediiumos"?
DIIIUIOMI — uncertain; possibly dative, "to Diiuios"? The repetition of VEDIIUMI suggests parallel invocations.

RISVM RISVM VEDIIUMÍ — "curse curse, to Vediiumos" (RISVM = "curse", imperative or noun?; repetition for emphasis)

AVDMON AVOTÓN — "hear the vow" or "hearing, having vowed" (AVDMON = imperative or participle of "hear"; AVOTÓN = past participle or noun, "vowed")

MAPONOS ARVERNORIGIIS — "Maponos of the Arverni kings" (MAPONOS = nominative or vocative, the god's name; ARVERNORIGIIS = genitive or dative, "of the Arverni kings")

sections.heading: MAPONOS and the Arverni
sections.body: MAPONOS ("divine youth" or "divine son") is a Gaulish god identified with Apollo in Roman interpretations. The name appears in dedications across Gaul and Britain. ARVERNORIGIIS means "of the Arverni kings". The Arverni were the dominant Gallic tribe of central Gaul; their king Vercingetorix led the final resistance to Caesar in 52 BCE. By 50 CE, when this tablet was inscribed, the Arverni were under Roman rule, but their memory and their gods endured. The invocation links Maponos to the old royal line.

sections.heading: Ritual repetition
sections.body:
The tablet repeats certain words for ritual effect:

RISVM RISVM — "curse curse"
VEDIIUMÍ (appears twice) — a name or epithet invoked twice

Repetition intensifies the invocation. This is common in magical texts across the ancient Mediterranean. Say a name twice and the spirit hears you louder. Say it three times and the binding is complete.

items.prompt: When and where was the Chamalières Tablet discovered?
items.answer: 1971, at the Source des Roches in Chamalières (Puy-de-Dôme, central France), in a sacred spring.

items.prompt: How many words are in the Chamalières Tablet?
items.answer: Sixty words, shorter than the Larzac Tablet but longer than most Gaulish inscriptions.
"Divine youth" or "divine son" — a Gaulish god identified with Apollo.
"Of the Arverni kings" — linking the god to the royal line of the Arverni tribe.
A dominant Gallic tribe of central Gaul. Their king Vercingetorix led the final resistance to Caesar in 52 BCE.
"Curse" — repeated for ritual emphasis (RISVM RISVM = "curse curse").

items.prompt: Why is repetition used in magical texts?
items.answer: To intensify the invocation. Repeating a name or command makes the binding stronger.
